name: São Miguel, Azores
summary: One volcanic island. Crater lakes, hot springs, tea fields, and a whale watch with a spare day in case the sea says no. Quiet, green, and a long way from both home airports.
why: April is mild rather than hot, the island is never a capital-city trip, and the wildlife is the educational event. Two bases are enough for two weeks. You do not need a second island.
distinctive: A green crater you can drive around, fumaroles in a town garden, and sperm whales that live offshore all year.
weather: A São Miguel climate guide puts a typical April near 18°C by day, 13°C at night, with roughly 80 mm of rain and a sea around 16°C. Cloud on the crater rims can sit there while the coast is clear. Waterproof layers are the packing list.
crowds: April is outside European summer. The island has busy viewpoints on clear afternoons and is otherwise quiet by mainland-Europe standards. Whale boats have a passenger limit, which is the crowd control.
natureExperiences: Sete Cidades and the twin lakes, on a clear window
Furnas, the lake, and the steaming ground in Terra Nostra
A whale-and-dolphin watch from Ponta Delgada or Vila Franca do Campo
The tea fields at Gorreana
age6: Lake shores, a garden with a warm pool, a tea factory, and a boat only if the sea is kind and the operator takes small children.
age12: The whale briefing, the crater viewpoints, and the hot-spring science.
age14: The same, plus the old whaling lookouts and why the hunt stopped. Faial's university boats are the deeper version, and they require a second island this plan does not take.
adults: Slow driving, cooking in a volcanic valley, and a landscape that changes with each ridge. Nightlife is not the product.
gettingAround: A car, or two. Roads are narrow, green and sometimes cow-paced. Portugal drives on the right. Do not add Terceira or Pico unless you are willing to lose a day to weather. Inter-island flights cancel.
meetingPoint: Ponta Delgada, almost always via Lisbon or another European hub. From Melbourne this is one of the longest journeys in the set. From India it is also a two- or three-flight day. The island is the reward after a hard journey, which is why it ranks lower on practicality.
visaAu: Same Schengen position as mainland Portugal. Australian passports are visa-free for a short stay, EES biometrics apply at the first Schengen entry, and ETIAS was not yet operating.
visaIn: Indian passports need a Schengen visa. If the whole trip is the Azores, Portugal is the country to apply to. The islands are not a separate visa.
disadvantages: The flight from Melbourne is the weakest logistics in the shortlist.
Rain and hill cloud will hide at least one famous view. The spare days are the plan, not a failure.
The sea is about 16°C. Swimming with dolphins is a separate, colder, rule-bound choice. Watching from the boat is the family default.
Two weeks on one island is quiet on purpose. If the 14-year-old needs cities, this is the wrong first choice.
uncertainties: Whale sightings. Visit Portugal says sperm whales and dolphins are a year-round possibility and that blue whales are often seen in spring between São Miguel and Santa Maria. Nothing is guaranteed, and boats cancel in rough seas.

name: Western Bhutan
summary: A regulated Himalayan kingdom in rhododendron season. Extraordinary and quiet. The fee, the flights and the walking are different for this group than for a couple travelling alone.
why: If the first priority is peaceful mountains and a culture the children have not met, Bhutan is the strongest match. April is before the monsoon and often flower season. The 6-year-old and the two passports are the reasons it is not the default winner.
distinctive: A national tourism policy that caps the feel of the place, dzongs above rivers, and a monastery on a cliff you can choose not to climb.
weather: April is spring in the western valleys, before the June monsoon. Days in Paro and Thimphu are often mild, nights are cold, and Punakha, lower down, is warmer. Rhododendrons are a spring event. Flower timing moves with the year.
crowds: Bhutan does not feel like a European capital in April. Festival dates follow the lunar calendar and can fill a town for a few days. The 2027 Paro Tshechu date was not published in this research. Recheck if you want a festival, or avoid it if you want the quiet version.
natureExperiences: The Punakha valley and its river confluence
A short ridge walk, not a trek
Chele La only if the road is clear and the 6-year-old is having a good day
Tiger's Nest from the cafeteria viewpoint if the full climb is too much
age6: Dzong courtyards, rivers, and short walks. Tiger's Nest has many stairs. The cafeteria viewpoint is a complete visit at age 6.
age12: The fortress architecture, archery if a demonstration is on, and a longer piece of the Tiger's Nest path with a turnaround point.
age14: The same, plus the idea of a country that charges visitors to stay small. They are old enough for that conversation.
adults: The quiet, the textiles, the food, and time with a guide who can explain what you are looking at.
gettingAround: Bhutan's tourism FAQ says a certified guide is mandatory, including beyond the border towns. Indian government guidance for Indian visitors also lists a guide, certified accommodation, insurance and transport. You can book the pieces yourself. Treks need an accredited guide or operator. This plan does not trek. Roads are slow and winding. Budget two or three hours for valleys that look close on a map.
meetingPoint: Paro. Flights are daylight only and cancel in cloud. Seats are limited. Indian travellers have more routing options, including via Delhi or Kolkata, and a land border that the Australian party does not use in the same way. The simple plan is that everyone flies into Paro. Book when the visa or permit is approved.
visaAu: Australian passports need a visa before travel. The Sustainable Development Fee for non-Indian adults was published as USD 100 per person per night under a discount running until 31 August 2027. Children from age 6 until they turn 12 pay half. Children 12 and over pay the adult fee. Under 6 pay nothing. So the 6-year-old is half, and the 12- and 14-year-olds are full, on whichever passport they hold. This is a fee fact, not a calculator, and it can change.
visaIn: Indian passports need an entry permit, not a visa. A passport or voter ID is required, and children under 18 need a passport or birth certificate and a guardian. The Indian SDF was published as Nu or INR 1,200 per adult per night, with the same child discounts. Apply ahead. Arrival processing can be slow.
disadvantages: The nightly fee is much higher on Australian passports than on Indian passports. The children who have turned 12 pay the adult rate for their passport.
Paro flights are the most fragile logistics in the set.
Altitude: Paro and Thimphu sit above about 2,200 metres. Punakha is the lower, kinder valley. Take the first day slowly.
A 6-year-old will not do a Himalayan trek. The trip has to be valleys and short walks, and that is still a wonderful trip.
uncertainties: Whether the USD 100 discount is still in force in April 2027. It was published through 31 August 2027.
2027 festival dates.
Which guide and hotel are certified when you book. Use services.bhutan.travel or the Department of Tourism list.

name: Plitvice and Istria, Croatia
summary: Waterfalls in a forest, then a slower peninsula. April is the waterfall month. It is not the month for island-hopping.
why: Plitvice in April has water and fewer people than July. Istria adds hill towns and a coast without asking the group to live on ferries. One country, two bases, a sensible fortnight.
distinctive: A chain of lakes pouring into each other on wooden walks, close to a peninsula of small towns that is calmer than Dubrovnik.
weather: Plitvice sits up in the forest and is cooler than the coast. A travel model of April there cited about 14°C by day and 6°C at night, with frequent rain. Istria is milder. The sea is not warm. Seasonal, not a forecast.
crowds: Park writers describe April as low to moderate, with a bump if your dates hit Easter week. Easter 2027 is 28 March, so mid-April should be past that bump. Timed tickets are now part of the park's crowd management. Summer is the packed season.
natureExperiences: Plitvice's lower lakes and one waterfall route, not every boardwalk
A second, shorter park morning
Istrian hill lanes and an olive grove
A coast walk in Rovinj or Poreč
age6: The boat and the easier boardwalks. Wooden paths get slippery. Hold hands. Leave before they are tired, even if you have paid for a long route.
age12: The lake system as a water cycle you can see, plus a fort or a hill town.
age14: The same, and the question of why the park now uses timed entry.
adults: The water, the food in Istria, and Roman Parentium in Poreč if you want one serious building.
gettingAround: A car, or two. Croatia drives on the right. Ferries to Hvar or Korčula are the wrong tool in April. Many island services are still thin.
meetingPoint: Zagreb is the straightforward airport, then a drive south to the lakes. Both families connect through Europe. Venice or Ljubljana are possible alternates and add a border.
visaAu: Croatia is Schengen. Australian passports are visa-free for a short stay. EES applies. ETIAS was not operating.
visaIn: Indian passports need a Schengen visa. Apply to Croatia if the nights are mostly there.
disadvantages: The boardwalks are the attraction and the fatigue. Do not plan two full route days back to back for age 6.
April is a poor month for the Dalmatian islands. This plan stays north on purpose.
The Melbourne journey is long.
Plitvice is famous. Timed entry and an early start are how you keep it pleasant.
uncertainties: 2027 ticket windows and which routes are open.
Rain. The park is wet even in a good April.
Ferry fantasies. Recheck Jadrolinija before adding any island.

It is a strong trip in May or June, and a compromised one for this group in April.
name: Georgia
summary: A wine-and-fortress capital and a high church under a snowy mountain. Held back for April access and the Indian visa.
why: The landscapes and the food are memorable, and the country is less travelled than Italy or Türkiye. April gives you Tbilisi and a cold Kazbegi day. It does not give you the high villages.
distinctive: A capital in a river gorge, and Gergeti Trinity Church under Mount Kazbek when the last road is open.
weather: A Georgia monthly guide puts Tbilisi near 19°C by day and 8°C at night in April, with more rain than in March. Kazbegi is about 10°C by day and near freezing at night. Svaneti is colder and wetter. The Abano Pass into Tusheti is usually shut until late May or June.
crowds: April is not a peak month. Tbilisi is a city, not a resort crush. Kazbegi has a busy church car park on clear days.
natureExperiences: The Kazbegi valley and Gergeti, if the road to the church is open
A city gorge walk in Tbilisi
The Mtskheta cathedral town as a half day
Not Tusheti and not Ushguli in April
age6: Tbilisi's sulphur baths district from the street, a cable car, and a short stop below Gergeti. No high pass.
age12: The church and the mountain story, plus the food.
age14: The same, and the old town's layers. They will feel the limit of the April map.
adults: Food and wine. The wine is not the children's itinerary.
gettingAround: A driver is wiser than two rental cars in April on the Military Highway. Georgia drives on the right. Distances are short and roads are slow.
meetingPoint: Tbilisi. Connections via Istanbul, the Gulf or Europe. Fine from India. Long from Melbourne.

name: South Coast, Iceland
regionLabel: Reykjavík, the Golden Circle and the south coast
summary: Waterfalls, a black coast and a glacier lagoon, in a month when the highlands are still shut and the weather is still winter's cousin. Magnificent, and a hard fortnight for a 6-year-old.
why: Choose this if dramatic scenery outranks comfort. April has long daylight and fewer visitors than July. It does not have pleasant spring weather, open highland roads, or easy walking for a mixed-age group.
distinctive: A coast where waterfalls, black sand and ice sit in one day's drive, and almost no trees to soften it.
weather: April is often about 1–7°C, wet, and windy. Daylight runs long. Highland F-roads stay closed into June or July. Natural ice caves on Vatnajökull close for the season. Some guided ice tunnels still run. This is the published shoulder-season pattern.
crowds: Fewer visitors than midsummer. The Golden Circle and Skógafoss still get buses. Easter can tighten hotels. Easter 2027 is 28 March, so early April can still feel the edge of it.
natureExperiences: Seljalandsfoss and Skógafoss from the safe paths
Reynisfjara from the cliff, not the waterline
Jökulsárlón and the diamond beach
A geothermal pool every day, which is the family constant
age6: Waterfall viewpoints, pools, and short stops. No black-sand wave games. No highland roads. No long glacier hikes.
age12: The lagoon, the earthquake-and-volcano story, and a pool with a waterslide if the town has one.
age14: The same landscapes, plus why the road reports matter. They can read road.is.
adults: The light, the weather as a character, and design in Reykjavík. This is not a relaxed trip.
gettingAround: A car, or two, with full insurance attention. Wind and ice are the driving story. Check road.is and vedur.is every morning. Do not plan the interior.
meetingPoint: Keflavík. Both families connect through Europe or sometimes the US or the UK. From Melbourne it is a long two-stop journey. From India, usually via Europe.

visaIn: Schengen visa via Iceland if Iceland is the main destination.
disadvantages: The weather fails the 'pleasant April' test.
F-roads and many famous hiking trails are shut or still technical.
Wind at the black beaches is a safety issue for children.
One week is enough. Two weeks needs pools, Reykjavík, and rest, or it becomes a grind.

name: Kyushu, Japan
summary: Volcanoes, a rural hot-spring valley, a restored castle town and a harbour city, tied together without the Kyoto blossom crush. Best if you travel after 8 April and leave before 29 April 2027.
why: The children get trains, food, myths and a real landscape. The adults get design, history and onsen towns. A group of seven is easier on trains and one rental car than in a string of European hire vans. Mid-April is the quiet part of Kyushu's spring.
distinctive: A giant caldera, a gorge tied to founding myths, and Nagasaki's layered history, in a part of Japan that most first trips skip.
weather: A family guide to Kyushu cites Fukuoka around 20°C by day and 12°C at night in April. That matches the usual spring pattern: mild, sometimes wet, good for walking. Confirm the year with the Japan Meteorological Agency.
crowds: Kyushu lowland cherries often peak in late March or the first days of April. In 2026, full bloom was recorded in the first week of April in Fukuoka, Kumamoto, Nagasaki and nearby cities. The first week also catches the end of Japanese spring break. Golden Week 2027 starts on Thursday 29 April. The useful gap is about 8–25 April.
natureExperiences: Mount Aso's grasslands, if volcanic-gas levels allow
Takachiho Gorge and its myth caves, as a long day rather than a new country
Yufuin's rural valley
Beppu's steaming vents, from the paths only
age6: Trains, castle grounds, a river or seaside promenade, and a private family bath. Public mixed onsen is not the plan.
age12: The Aso caldera, Takachiho's story, castle museums, and choosing the day's noodles.
age14: Nagasaki's history, in the dose they can handle, plus the rail network itself. This is the destination where the 14-year-old has the most to do.
adults: Food, design, onsen etiquette, and two serious histories: a castle town and an international port. Kyoto is not required.
gettingAround: Trains between the cities. One rental car for the Aso and Takachiho days, because rural buses will exhaust a group of seven. Japan drives on the left, like both families. An International Driving Permit is worth confirming with the rental company rather than assuming.
meetingPoint: Fukuoka (Hakata). Both parties usually connect via Seoul, Singapore, Hong Kong or Tokyo. Direct Fukuoka flights from India or Melbourne should be treated as unconfirmed until the 2027 schedule is published.
visaAu: Australian passports do not need a visa for a short tourist stay of up to 90 days. Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists Australia among the visa-exempt nationalities.
visaIn: Indian passports are not on Japan's visa-exempt list. Apply through the Japanese embassy or consulate that covers the applicant's home city, usually via their visa centre. Document lists and processing times change. Start months ahead.
disadvantages: The first week of April and anything from 29 April onward are the wrong weeks.
Takachiho is a long drive. It is the one demanding transfer in an otherwise gentle route.
Public baths are often not set up for a mixed-age family. Book a room with a private bath.
Cherry blossom is mostly over in the cities by mid-April. Come for green hills and late flowers, not a hanami festival.
uncertainties: JR Kyushu times for 2027.
Whether Aso is open to visitors that week. Gas levels close the crater rim without much notice.
International seats out of Nagasaki. If they are poor, spend the last night back in Fukuoka.

name: Jeju and Gyeongju, South Korea
regionLabel: A volcanic island and a museum without walls
summary: A lava island for the first week and a tomb-and-temple city for the second. Mild April, excellent for children, less wild than Kyushu's volcano country.
why: Korea is easy with children: food you can share, museums, a volcanic island, and trains. Jeju keeps the nature. Gyeongju gives the 12- and 14-year-olds history without Seoul's scale. It sits just behind Kyushu because the landscape is softer and the Indian visa is still required.
distinctive: A shield volcano you do not need to summit, lava tubes, and a capital of an old kingdom scattered through green mounds.
weather: Jeju in April is mild, often the mid-teens, windy, and not beach-swimming weather. Hallasan's upper trails can still hold snow or ice. Seasonal expectation.
crowds: Early April coincides with blossom season and domestic travel. Mid-April is kinder. Jeju's big sights have car-park crowds on weekends. Gyeongju is calmer than Seoul.
natureExperiences: A coastal volcanic cone such as Seongsan, without a dangerous cliff edge
Manjanggul lava tube
A short Hallasan approach, not the summit
The green mounds of Gyeongju by bike or on foot
age6: Lava tube, folk village, beach walks, and the tumuli park. No Hallasan summit.
age12: The lava-tube geology and the idea of a kingdom you can still see in the landscape.
age14: Gyeongju's museum, plus the science museum or a planetarium if you add a short Seoul buffer. This plan keeps Seoul optional.
adults: Food, a walkable history city, and an island that is not a resort week.
gettingAround: Fly into Jeju. A car, or two, on the island. Then a flight to Busan or Seoul and a train to Gyeongju. Korea drives on the right. Trains are the easy part.
meetingPoint: Seoul or Jeju. Seoul is the easier ticket for both countries. A domestic hop to Jeju is about an hour. Indian passports need a visa. Australian passports were inside a K-ETA exemption through 31 December 2026. From 1 January 2027 that exemption was described as ending, so April 2027 likely needs a K-ETA. Recheck the official K-ETA site.
visaAu: Short tourism stays have been visa-free for Australians, with K-ETA temporarily waived through 31 December 2026. Plan on a K-ETA for April 2027 unless Korea extends the waiver. Children have had age exemptions from K-ETA in past notices. Read the current rule for each traveller.
visaIn: Indian passports are not K-ETA eligible. The Korean consulate in Mumbai states that Indian nationals need a visa. Apply through the official mission.
disadvantages: Hallasan's summit is the wrong goal with a 6-year-old in April.
The scenery is lovely and less dramatic than Aso, Fiordland or Jiuzhaigou.
Blossom week and weekends are the busy times.

name: Bergen and the western fjords, Norway
summary: A harbour city and one famous railway down to a fjord. April can be beautiful and it is also when many of Norway's great mountain roads and hikes are still shut.
why: Choose it for the railway and the fjord light, not for hiking. The children will remember the train and the waterfalls. They will not get Trolltunga, Geiranger by road, or a mild week.
distinctive: A 20-kilometre branch line from a high railway down to a fjord, with a waterfall stop, in a country that is still waking up in April.
weather: Bergen in April is often near 10°C by day and a few degrees at night, and it rains. Snow remains on the mountains. Seasonal pattern.
crowds: April is quiet compared with June and July. Easter week is the Norwegian mountain holiday. Easter 2027 ends on 29 March, so the first days of April can still be odd. Cities are open. Many mountain lodges are not in full summer mode.

name: South Island, New Zealand
summary: Autumn lakes, a high mountain, and a fiord, linked by a slow road trip. Four bases. The Melbourne party has the shortest flight of any option in this set.
why: April is a real season here, not a gap between seasons. The walks, boat days and towns used in this plan are generally open, the colours in Central Otago are the reason to come, and summer crowds have dropped. Both families already drive on the left.
distinctive: Glacial lakes under a single mountain range, a dark-sky basin, and a fiord reached through a long mountain road. The trip is the landscape itself.
weather: Typical April on the South Island is mild by day and cold at night. A commonly cited range is about 8–19°C, with Queenstown and Central Otago often nearer 16°C by day and about 5°C at night. Fiordland is wetter than Mackenzie. This is a seasonal pattern, not a forecast.
crowds: March still feels busy. April and May are when tour traffic and prices ease, according to South Island seasonal guides. Milford and the Wānaka lakefront still draw people on fine days. They are not July-in-Dubrovnik crowds.
natureExperiences: Aoraki / Mount Cook and the Tasman Valley, with Hooker Valley only if the track is open
Lake Tekapo and the Mackenzie dark-sky basin
Lake Wānaka and the Arrowtown autumn trees
Milford Sound by boat, with Doubtful Sound as the quieter backup
age6: Lakefronts, short flat walks, a boat cruise, and the Te Anau glowworm cave. Skip bungy, canyon swings and long alpine tracks.
age12: The glowworm cave, a fiord cruise, Mount John if the weather is kind, and a choice of one bigger walk with an adult.
age14: The same landscapes, plus the geology of the Alps and the option to split off for a harder walk while the younger child stays by the lake.
adults: Driving days with real scenery, dark skies, and time in small towns. Māori place names and glacier stories are part of the trip, not a separate city break.
gettingAround: This is a road trip. Seven people plus bags means two cars, not one. Book a child seat for the 6-year-old and confirm the rental rule. The open-jaw that fits the map is into Christchurch and out of Queenstown.
meetingPoint: Christchurch. Melbourne–Christchurch is often about 3.5–4 hours nonstop. The Indian party connects through a hub such as Singapore, Kuala Lumpur or an Australian city. Confirm the 2027 timetable before treating any flight as direct.
visaAu: Australian citizens travelling on an Australian passport do not need a visa or an NZeTA. Immigration New Zealand says an Australian Resident Visa is normally granted on arrival if character requirements are met.
visaIn: Indian passports are not visa-waiver passports. They need a visitor visa before travel, not an NZeTA. Tourism New Zealand's India page says the passport should be valid for at least 3 months after the planned departure from New Zealand. Early 2026 processing for Indian visitor visas averaged about 7 working days, with an 84% approval rate from January to April 2026. That is a recent statistic, not a promise for 2027.
disadvantages: The Indian party has a long flight and a real visa application. Do not buy the non-refundable tickets until that visa is approved.
Culture and ancient history are lighter here than in Türkiye, Japan or Sichuan.
Milford is a full day in the car and on a boat. The road closes for snow, avalanche control and crashes.
April is not ski season. Do not plan the trip around snow sports.
uncertainties: 2027 airfares, rental-vehicle supply for a group of seven, and the Milford Road status on the day.

name: Northern Portugal
summary: A river city, a green wine valley, and Portugal's only national park. April is mild, the waterfalls are full, and you never need Lisbon.
why: It is the relaxed European alternative: beautiful, cultural, and easier to pace than Italy or Spain's famous cities. The 6-year-old can do boats, short trails and a city of tiles. The older two get the river terraces and the park.
distinctive: Terrace vineyards falling into a deep river, and a granite mountain park with spring waterfalls an hour or two from a real city.
weather: April in northern Portugal is mild, often the high teens, with some rain and green hills. The Douro can be warmer in the afternoon. The Atlantic is still cool for swimming. Seasonal expectation, not a forecast.
crowds: Porto's riverfront has visitors in April and is calmer than summer. The Douro quintas and Gerês trails are the quiet part. Easter 2027 is over by 29 March, so a mid-April trip misses Holy Week.
natureExperiences: A Douro boat between the terraces
Peneda-Gerês waterfalls and a short trail

age6: The river cruise, a short Gerês walk, and Porto's trams or a river-level promenade. Skip long granite scrambles.

age14: The same, plus how the terraces were built and a look at port wine from the outside of the process. Tasting is for adults.
adults: Porto on foot, a valley that is working farmland, and long lunches. This is the comfortable trip.
gettingAround: Train or metro in Porto. A car, ideally two, for the Douro and Gerês. Portugal drives on the right. The Douro train line is a scenic alternative for a day without the car, if the 2027 timetable still serves the village you choose.
meetingPoint: Porto. Both families connect through Europe or the Middle East. Less painful than the Azores, still a long haul from Melbourne.
visaAu: Schengen short-stay visa-free, EES biometrics on entry, ETIAS not yet operating at the time of research.
visaIn: Schengen visa, applied to Portugal if Portugal is the main stay.

name: Sichuan, China
summary: Pandas at opening time, a bronze-age mystery pit, an ancient irrigation works, and a valley of coloured lakes. The most unusual education in this set, with a visa question mark for 2027.
why: The 12- and 14-year-olds get Sanxingdui and Dujiangyan, which are real science and history. The 6-year-old gets pandas and a boardwalk valley. You can do it from Chengdu plus two side bases, by train and one short flight.
distinctive: A conservation centre for giant pandas beside an archaeological site that rewrote early Chinese history, and a high valley of mineral lakes.
weather: Chengdu in April is often mild and cloudy, roughly the mid-teens to mid-20s. Jiuzhaigou's valley is cooler. One spring guide cited about 11–24°C there in a past April. Nights at the park towns are cold. This is seasonal, not a forecast.
crowds: Jiuzhaigou's own 2026 peak-season notice set a daily capacity of 41,000 and full-valley opening from 1 April, with entry 08:00–14:00. Capacity that high means the park can still feel busy. The calmer aim is the middle of April, after Qingming and before the Labour Day holiday. The 2027 holiday dates need the State Council notice.
natureExperiences: Jiuzhaigou's lakes and waterfalls, using the park buses rather than trying to walk the whole valley
Dujiangyan and the wooded paths of nearby Qingcheng Mountain, kept short
A dawn visit to the Chengdu panda base
Leshan's river cliff and giant Buddha, seen without rushing the same day as Chengdu
age6: Pandas first, then the Jiuzhaigou buses and short boardwalks. Skip Huanglong. It sits higher, around 3,000 metres.
age12: Sanxingdui's masks, the panda science, and the coloured lakes.
age14: Dujiangyan's 2,000-year-old flood works, Sanxingdui, and the question of how a landscape makes lakes that colour.
adults: Teahouses, the archaeology, and a national park that does not look like anywhere else. Sichuan food is spicy. Ask for mild plates for the children.
gettingAround: High-speed rail for Leshan. A flight of about an hour from Chengdu to Jiuzhai Huanglong Airport, then a ground transfer of about 1–1.5 hours. Confirm both in 2027. China drives on the right. You do not need a car for this plan.
meetingPoint: Chengdu Tianfu or Shuangliu. Melbourne usually connects via a Chinese or Southeast Asian hub. Indian cities have more one-stop options. Meet in Chengdu and give the long-haul party a free first afternoon.
visaAu: In February 2026, China's visa-free entry for ordinary Australian passports, for up to 30 days and for tourism, was described as running until 31 December 2026. April 2027 is after that date. Unless Beijing extends it, the Australian party will need a visa too. Do not book as if the waiver still exists.
visaIn: India was not on that visa-free list. Indian passports should plan on a tourist visa. The 240-hour transit scheme is not a way to spend two weeks in Sichuan, and Jiuzhaigou's prefecture has been excluded from some transit areas. Use a proper visa.
disadvantages: The Australian visa waiver, as published, expires before this trip. Both passport groups should plan on visas until an extension is official.
Jiuzhaigou's entrance is about 1,990 metres. The park says altitude sickness is uncommon and still possible. Take the first afternoon slowly. Skip Huanglong with a 6-year-old.
The food is part of the pleasure and a problem for cautious children. Build in plain rice, dumplings and mild dishes.
English is thinner on the ground than in Japan or New Zealand. Offline maps and the hotel card in Chinese matter.

name: Slovenia
regionLabel: Ljubljana, Bohinj, Soča and the Karst
summary: A small country of a quiet lake, an emerald river, and a cave you enter by train. Two weeks is enough if you stay in four bases and stay off the high passes.
why: It gives the group Alps, water and a genuine science cave without the scale of Italy or France. Lake Bohinj is the calmer base. Postojna is the hour all three children can share. April is green and cool, with rain built into the plan.
distinctive: A karst underworld and a river the colour of glass, in a country you can cross in an afternoon and should not.
weather: April in Slovenia is green, changeable and often wet. Valley days are cool rather than cold, often around the mid-teens, and mountain nights are colder. The sea at Piran is too cold for swimming. High trails and passes can still hold snow. Treat any specific degree figure as a seasonal expectation.
crowds: Lake Bled is the busy postcard. Bohinj, Kobarid and the Karst are calmer. Easter 2027 is 28 March, so a mid-April trip misses Holy Week. European school holidays can still spill into the first days of April.
natureExperiences: Lake Bohinj and the Savica waterfall at an easy pace
The Soča river from Kobarid or Bovec, without relying on the Vršič Pass
Kozjak waterfall near Kobarid
Postojna Cave, 10°C inside, by cave train
age6: The cave train, a lake shore, a castle courtyard at Predjama, and Ljubljana's old town at walking pace. No rafting.
age12: Postojna's karst exhibition, the Soča colour, and the Kobarid World War I museum.
age14: The same museum, Škocjan Caves if you want a wilder and steeper cave than Postojna, and the map of a country this small.
adults: Ljubljana's river, the history in the Soča valley, and food that is hearty rather than formal. Wine is optional and not the children's day.
gettingAround: A car is the right tool. Two cars for seven people. Slovenia drives on the right, which is new for both families. A vignette is required on motorways. Do not plan the trip over the Vršič Pass. In April 2026 it was not described as a full winter closure, and a works notice covered May to November 2026. Snow can still shut it. Use the lower road via Tolmin.
meetingPoint: Ljubljana is the simple meeting airport, with fewer long-haul seats than Vienna, Zurich or Venice. Both parties should expect a European connection. Melbourne is a long way. The Indian city with the better Europe fare can decide the Indian departure airport.
visaAu: Australian passports can enter Slovenia visa-free for a short Schengen stay. Since 10 April 2026 the EU Entry/Exit System has been recording biometrics at the Schengen border. You do not apply for EES in advance. ETIAS, the online authorisation for visa-free passports, was not operating as of this research. The EU said it would announce a start date months ahead. Recheck before 2027.
visaIn: Indian passports need a Schengen visa. Apply to Slovenia if Slovenia is the main destination. Appointments, insurance and funds rules are the slow part. Start several months ahead and use the official consulate or VFS channel, not a forum checklist from a previous year.
disadvantages: Both families fly a long way for a small country. The payoff is that you stop rushing once you land.
April is not swimming weather and not high-alpine hiking weather.
Rafting and canyoning on the Soča are a warmer-month activity. Cold, high spring water is a reason to watch the river, not ride it.
Lake Bled's famous view is real and busy. Sleep at Bohinj.
uncertainties: Vršič and other alpine roads in April 2027. Check promet.si.
Vintgar Gorge's opening date. It is often seasonal. Do not build a day on it until the park confirms 2027.
Whether ETIAS will be in force for the Australian passports.

crowds: Taipei is a working city. Taroko, when open, has busy viewpoints. Not researched as a crowd calendar.
natureExperiences: Alishan or a forest railway if you go without Taroko

name: Cappadocia and the Aegean, Türkiye
summary: Three bases: a city on two shores, a valley of rock cones, and an ancient port. April is mild, green, and before the real heat. The Indian visa is the complication.
why: It is the clearest mix of landscape and deep history that is pleasant in April. Children can share the fairy chimneys, a cave hotel, and Ephesus at opening time. The pace stays at three bases, with domestic flights instead of a cross-country drive.
distinctive: Volcanic rock valleys you can walk through, and a Roman city that is still a street plan rather than a single ruin.
weather: Long-term station normals cited from the Turkish State Meteorological Service put April near 17°C by day and 9°C at night in Istanbul, about 16°C and 5°C in Cappadocia, and about 21°C and 11°C on the Aegean–Mediterranean coast. The sea is still about 18–19°C. Cappadocia nights are cold. This is a normal, not a forecast.
crowds: April is before the summer crush at Ephesus and Göreme, and it is not empty. Istanbul is always busy. Balloons fill the sky on flyable mornings. 23 April is National Sovereignty and Children's Day. ANZAC Day is Sunday 25 April 2027 at Gallipoli, which this plan does not include.
natureExperiences: Rose Valley or Love Valley at a family pace, from Ürgüp or Ortahisar rather than only Göreme
A sunrise viewpoint over the cones, whether or not a balloon flies
The travertine idea of Pamukkale only as a swap, not as an extra dash
Şirince's hills above Selçuk
age6: Cave-hotel mornings, short valley walks, a pottery wheel in Avanos, and the flat parts of Ephesus. Underground cities only until the child wants to turn around.
age12: Ephesus as a city you can read, the open-air museum's churches, and one balloon morning if the operator accepts their height.
age14: Hagia Sophia and the Basilica Cistern, Ephesus, and the engineering of the rock valleys. The Rahmi M. Koç Museum in Istanbul is the science stop.
adults: The layers of Istanbul, the sculpted valleys, and a Roman city in good light. Evenings are for food, not a new monument.
gettingAround: Fly Istanbul to Cappadocia (Nevşehir or Kayseri) and Cappadocia to İzmir, then a short transfer to Selçuk. Each flight is often about 1–1.5 hours. Book seven seats early. A car helps in Cappadocia. Türkiye drives on the right. Two cars if you drive as a group.
meetingPoint: Istanbul is the easy common airport for Melbourne and for major Indian cities. The Indian departure city can stay undecided until you know which Indian airport has the better Istanbul fare.
visaAu: Ordinary Australian passports are exempt from a visa for tourism up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Official Turkish foreign-ministry guidance and Smartraveller both say this. Passport validity rules still apply.
visaIn: Ordinary, special and service Indian passports need a visa. The official e-Visa is available only if the traveller also holds a valid Schengen, US, UK or Ireland visa or residence permit, and that document must still be valid on the day they enter Türkiye. Without that supporting visa, the path is a sticker visa through a Turkish mission. Use only evisa.gov.tr if you are eligible. Many lookalike sites are not the government.
disadvantages: The Indian visa is conditional. If nobody in that party holds a supporting Schengen, US, UK or Ireland visa, the e-Visa is not the path.
Istanbul and Göreme are famous. The plan uses quieter bases and early hours. It does not make them empty.
Balloon rules are set by operators. Many ask for about age 6 and enough height to see over the basket, often described around 4 feet 6 inches. The 6-year-old is on the borderline.
The sea is cool for swimming. Do not sell this as a beach holiday.
uncertainties: Which visa path the Indian passports will actually qualify for in 2027.
Balloon fly rates. Spring mornings are good and still get cancelled for wind.

gain: History and strange scenery in the same fortnight, in weather that suits ruins and walking.
miss: A simple visa for Indian passports, and the kind of empty nature you get in Fiordland or Bhutan.
stretch16: Add a free day in Ürgüp and a free day in Selçuk. Do not add Antalya and Pamukkale and Gallipoli.

days.experience: Land and walk one neighbourhood only. Galata or a Bosphorus ferry if the light is good.
days.optional: No palace on day one
days.highlight: The water between two shores
days.kids: The ferry is the right first activity.
days.transfer: Istanbul is the meeting airport. Allow a long transfer from the airport into the city.
days.seasonal: April showers are normal. Shoes that can get wet.
days.wet: A covered bazaar street and a pudding shop, kept short.

days.experience: Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque courtyard, and the Basilica Cistern.
days.optional: Gülhane Park afterwards
days.highlight: One ridge of monuments, then a park
days.kids: The cistern is the one the 6-year-old is most likely to remember. Leave when they fade.
days.transfer: Walk and tram. Buy museum tickets the way the official sites tell you to in 2027.
days.seasonal: Go at opening. Midday is the crowded hour.
days.wet: The cistern and the mosques are the wet-weather plan.

days.experience: Rahmi M. Koç Museum, an industrial and transport museum on the Golden Horn.
days.optional: A short Bosphorus hop
days.highlight: Engines, submarines and hands-on halls. This is the science day.
days.kids: Built for the 6- and 12-year-olds, and still interesting at 14.
days.transfer: A short taxi or bus from Sultanahmet or Karaköy.
days.seasonal: Check the museum's closed day before you lock the date.
days.wet: Stay here. It is indoors.

days.experience: Princes' Islands by ferry. Walk or hire a bicycle, not a packed carriage.
days.optional: Nothing else that evening
days.highlight: A wooded island without cars, an hour from the city
days.kids: The ferry plus a short ride. Büyükada's hills are steep if you try to see everything.
days.transfer: Ferries leave from the city's Asian and European docks. Allow most of the day.
days.seasonal: 23 April can be festive and busy. A weekday is calmer.
days.wet: Swap for the Istanbul Modern or a second pass at the Koç Museum.

days.experience: A free half day, then the flight to Cappadocia if the afternoon plane is the sane one.
days.optional: Spice Market in twenty minutes, not two hours
days.highlight: Leaving the city before it becomes the whole trip
days.kids: Pack in the morning so the airport is not a panic.
days.transfer: Istanbul to Nevşehir or Kayseri is often about 1–1.5 hours, plus a 1-hour ground transfer. Confirm which airport your hotel actually meets.
days.seasonal: Book seven seats when the Indian visas are clear, not before.
days.wet: Fly anyway.

days.experience: Arrive, look at the valley from the hotel, and stop.
days.optional: A sunset viewpoint a short walk away
days.highlight: The first sight of the cones in evening light
days.kids: Cave rooms are the adventure.
days.transfer: Included in the arrival day if you flew. If this is a 10-day trip, fly on the morning after the Koç Museum instead.
days.seasonal: Ortahisar and Ürgüp are calmer bases than the centre of Göreme.
days.wet: The hotel and a short look from a terrace.

days.experience: Sunrise viewpoint. A balloon only if the operator has confirmed the 6-year-old's height and the wind is kind.
days.optional: A pottery workshop in Avanos in the afternoon
days.highlight: The valleys at dawn, from the ground if the balloon does not fly
days.kids: Have a non-flying plan the 6-year-old will like. A cold launch field at 5am is hard even when the flight goes.
days.transfer: Hotels transfer you to the launch field. Recheck the operator's age and height rule.
days.seasonal: Spring flyable mornings are common and not guaranteed. Cancellations are a safety decision.
days.wet: Sleep in and do the pottery and a valley overlook by car.

days.experience: Göreme Open-Air Museum at opening, then a short valley walk.
days.optional: Uçhisar castle viewpoint
days.highlight: Rock-cut churches, then a walk among the cones
days.kids: The museum is a series of small caves. The 6-year-old will do some of it. The valley walk should be the easy one.
days.transfer: A short drive. Go in your own car or a driver, early.
days.seasonal: Midday tour buses are the crowd. Opening time is the tactic.
days.wet: The museum is partly sheltered. Skip the valley mud.

days.experience: One underground city, Kaymaklı or Derinkuyu, and an easy afternoon.
days.optional: Turn around after the first level
days.highlight: A hidden city carved down into the rock
days.kids: Claustrophobic, steep and dim. The 14-year-old may love it. The 6-year-old needs an exit plan.
days.transfer: Under an hour by car.
days.seasonal: Do not do both underground cities.
days.wet: This is already indoors.

days.experience: A free day. Repeat the valley you liked, or do nothing.
days.optional: A picnic overlook
days.highlight: The landscape without a ticket
days.kids: Let them climb the hotel rocks and draw the chimneys.
days.transfer: None.
days.seasonal: Pigeon Valley and Rose Valley have uneven ground. Pick the short version.
days.wet: Hotel hammam or a long lunch in Ürgüp.

days.experience: Fly to İzmir and transfer to Selçuk. Evening in a small town.
days.optional: Stork nests on the aqueduct, if the birds are in
days.highlight: A town built beside the ruins, not a resort strip
days.kids: The storks, if present, are the arrival story.
days.transfer: Cappadocia to İzmir is often about 1.5 hours, then under an hour to Selçuk. Confirm.
days.seasonal: April is a strong month for Ephesus because the heat has not arrived.
days.wet: Settle in. The ruins are tomorrow at opening.

days.experience: Ephesus at opening, and the Terrace Houses only if the older children are still curious.
days.optional: Ephesus Museum in the afternoon, which is small
days.highlight: The Library of Celsus and a marble street
days.kids: Age 6 will do the main street and then need shade and a snack. Ages 12 and 14 can go further.
days.transfer: A few kilometres from Selçuk. Taxis or a driver are simpler than parking.
days.seasonal: The stone is bright and hot even in April if you arrive at noon.
days.wet: Go anyway. Marble is slippery. The museum is the backup.

days.experience: Şirince village in the hills.
days.optional: A short orchard walk
days.highlight: A quieter village above the ruins
days.kids: Fruit juice, lanes, and a limit on how far you climb.
days.transfer: About 15–20 minutes from Selçuk.
days.seasonal: The village is small. Leave before it feels crowded.
days.wet: The Ephesus Museum, or a pastry shop in Selçuk.

days.experience: A last easy morning and the flight from İzmir.
days.optional: Priene or Miletus only if this is the 14-day version and the children ask for more ruins
days.highlight: Leaving from the Aegean, not backtracking through Istanbul unless the fare demands it
days.kids: Do not add a ruin on departure morning.
days.transfer: Selçuk to İzmir airport is under an hour. Seven seats on the long haul home need an early booking.
days.seasonal: Gallipoli on 25 April 2027 is a separate, solemn, crowded pilgrimage. It is not part of this route.
days.wet: Go to the airport.
